Per day, a number or a range like 1-3 (r: Per day, a number or a range like 1-3 (random each day). Empty = the general setting "Devices: times per day".
How long each time, e.g. 30-90. Empty =: How long each time, e.g. 30-90. Empty = the general settings "Devices run at least / at most (min)".
When you come home: \"automatic\" switch: When you come home: "automatic" switches devices such as the TV off and leaves lamps on, so nobody stands in the dark. Or always switch off, or leave on.
Choose how messages reach your phone – T: Choose how messages reach your phone – Telegram, Pushover, WhatsApp, e-mail … The matching adapter must already be installed and set up in ioBroker. To try it: press "Save" at the bottom first (the assistant stays open), then "Send test message".
Only messengers that Home Guard supports: Only messengers that Home Guard supports and that are installed can be chosen; the fields the messenger needs appear in its row. Other messengers can be reached via the ioBroker notification manager.
Devices that the automatic search found: Devices that the automatic search found by their role are listed here without a tick – tick the ones that should be watched, then their settings appear.
Doors and windows you open while at home: Doors and windows you open while at home
Detectors inside the house: motion and p: Detectors inside the house: motion and presence sensors, light barriers, a camera with motion detection, an interior door. Only watched in full protection, i.e. when nobody is at home. Any state works – it raises the alarm as soon as it reports true, a number above 0 or "open". The easiest way is a function – everything in it is watched, and sensors you add to it later are picked up by themselves.
Everything that reports a break-in from: Everything that reports a break-in from outside: door and window contacts, window handles, glass break, vibration or roller shutter sensors. They raise an alarm in every way of being armed – full, perimeter and night protection. Any state works – it raises the alarm as soon as it reports true, a number above 0 or "open". The easiest way is a function – everything in it is watched, and sensors you add to it later are picked up by themselves.
Never an alarm – just a message, e.g. \": Never an alarm – just a message, e.g. "garden gate opened", "post in the letter box" or "somebody rang". The easiest way is a function – everything in it is watched, and sensors you add to it later are picked up by themselves.
Single devices without a function, and e: Single devices without a function, and exceptions, come in on the page "Alarm system: single sensors & exceptions".
Smoke, heat, water, gas or CO detectors: Smoke, heat, water, gas or CO detectors – and a panic button. They are always active, also when the alarm system is off. Choose whether they only send a message, also speak, or raise a full alarm with siren; a panic button belongs on "full alarm" (single devices get their own reaction on the page "Alarm system: single sensors & exceptions"). Any state works – it raises the alarm as soon as it reports true, a number above 0 or "open". The easiest way is a function – everything in it is watched, and sensors you add to it later are picked up by themselves.
E.g. the bedroom window you tilt at nigh: E.g. the bedroom window you tilt at night: add it on the page "Alarm system: single sensors & exceptions" and tick "ignore at home". It stays watched in full protection (nobody at home) and is ignored in perimeter and night protection.
Outer skin only: watched in full protect: Outer skin only: watched in full protection, ignored in perimeter and night protection (e.g. the bedroom window you tilt at night)
\"delayed\": entry delay instead of an i: "delayed": entry delay instead of an immediate alarm (the door you come in through). "inverted": the sensor reports open as false. "ignore at home" (outer skin only): watched in full protection, ignored in perimeter and night protection – e.g. the bedroom window you tilt at night.
The table is for four things: 1. a devic: The table is for four things: 1. a device that is in no function – add a row with the area it belongs to. 2. a device from a function that should behave differently (other area, delayed, inverted, own reaction) – add the same state again with its settings; the row wins over the function. 3. a device from a function that should not be watched – add a row and untick "Active". 4. a door or window you open while at home (e.g. the bedroom window) – add a row and tick "ignore at home". Tick "inverted" only if a sensor reports the wrong way round (shows "closed" when it is open).

Nothing to test – nothing is set up for: Nothing to test – nothing is set up for the ticked parts
The \"notification-manager\" adapter is: The "notification-manager" adapter is installed and running. Which messengers get the alarms is set in its settings.
The "notification-manager" adapter is installed but not running. Start the instance so that alarms are forwarded.
The "notification-manager" adapter is not installed. Without it alarms only appear in the bell of the admin and go to no messenger. Install it under "Adapters" and set up the messengers there.
✔ Amazon Echo (Alexa) – for the alarm or: ✔ Amazon Echo (Alexa) – for the alarm or radio in the simulation – already set up
Exception: doors and windows with the ti: Exception: doors and windows with the tick "ignore at home" are only watched in full protection (see below).
Doors and windows with the tick \"ignore: Doors and windows with the tick "ignore at home" are not watched at night.
Window handles with 0 = closed, 1 = tilt: Window handles with 0 = closed, 1 = tilted, 2 = open: tilted is no alarm in perimeter and night protection, fully open is. In full protection tilted counts as open.
Arm and leave them out until they are cl: Arm and leave them out until they are closed
Disarms like the PIN, but sends a silent: Disarms like the PIN, but sends a silent alarm to the messengers – for when somebody forces you to switch off. Must differ from the PIN.
Checks that every sensor works: start it: Checks that every sensor works: start it while the system is disarmed, then open every door and window and walk past every motion detector. Home Guard ticks off every sensor that reports and tells you at the end which ones stayed silent (empty battery, wrong state). Arming ends it.
\"tilted is OK\" (outer skin, window han: "tilted is OK" (outer skin, window handles with 0 = closed, 1 = tilted, 2 = open): tilted is no alarm in perimeter and night protection, fully open is – in full protection tilted counts as open.
Walk test started – trigger every sensor: Walk test started – trigger every sensor now
The walk test only runs while the alarm: The walk test only runs while the alarm system is disarmed
No walk test is running – the last resul: No walk test is running – the last result is in the logbook
Walk test finished: %s of %s sensors rep: Walk test finished: %s of %s sensors reported
Simulation stays off until armed again o: Simulation stays off until armed again or somebody leaves (recommended)
Simulation may run again after some minu: Simulation may run again after some minutes when nobody is at home
Arm again after some minutes when nobody: Arm again after some minutes when nobody is at home
Disarming means somebody comes home – of: Disarming means somebody comes home – often before the phone is in the Wi-Fi. So the presence simulation stops at once. Here you choose what happens when the presence detection still says nobody is at home.
⚠ Careful: with an empty or forgotten ph: ⚠ Careful: with an empty or forgotten phone you count as not at home – the system then arms itself while you are inside, and opening a door triggers the alarm. Only choose this if everybody reliably carries a phone that the presence detection sees.
Plays the alarm sound and the text once: Plays the alarm sound and the text once on the chosen Echo – with the volume and sound from the Echo table – and then sets the volume back.
Sent to %s – the sound should play in a: Sent to %s – the sound should play in a few seconds
The PIN protects switching off: with a P: The PIN protects switching off: with a PIN, only somebody who knows it can disarm the alarm system – in the panel, on the wall tablet or on the phone. Without a PIN, anybody who can reach the panel can switch it off – a burglar too. Choose 4 to 6 digits that are not easy to guess (no birthday, no 1234). The options below appear once a PIN is entered.
On: arming also asks for the PIN in the: On: arming also asks for the PIN in the panel. Arming by state (control.mode, scripts, automations) is then refused. Off: anybody can arm – harmless, because arming never weakens the protection. Usually leave this off.
On: switching off by state (control.mode: On: switching off by state (control.mode, control.off, scripts, a button in another visualisation) is refused – only the PIN written to control.pin, the panel or the door lock disarm. Recommended when other systems or visualisations can write to ioBroker states. Off: every script and every visualisation can switch off without the PIN.
When the alarm sounds, it can be stopped: When the alarm sounds, it can be stopped in two ways. Switch off (disarm): the alarm system is off – this always needs the PIN. Acknowledge: sirens, alarm lights and Echos go quiet, but the alarm system stays armed – any further sensor triggers the alarm again at once, without entry delay.
Acknowledge without PIN (default): anybo: Acknowledge without PIN (default): anybody at the panel can stop a false alarm, e.g. children or a guest without the PIN. A burglar who presses "Acknowledge" only gets silence: the system stays armed, the next door or motion detector raises the alarm again, and you get the message "Alarm acknowledged – without PIN". Acknowledge with PIN: only somebody with the PIN can silence the alarm – choose this if it should keep sounding until somebody with the PIN is there.
On: only somebody with the PIN can silen: On: only somebody with the PIN can silence a running alarm (keypad in the panel, or the PIN written to control.ackPin; control.ack is refused). Off: anybody at the panel can acknowledge – sirens, lights and Echos stop, the system stays armed, and you get the message "Alarm acknowledged – without PIN".
